names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 22 iunie, «Sfântul Ierarh Grigorie Dascălul, Mitropolitul Țării Românești»; the form is the name and the byname the line gives, the rest being rank and see.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Διδάσκαλος ο Βατοπαιδινός», with the rank word left off. The two bynames the line adds, ο Διδάσκαλος, the Teacher, and ο Βατοπαιδινός, of Vatopedi, are left off the stored form as the see and the epithets are elsewhere.

death.note: doxologia.ro's page for the synaxis of the Athonite saints prints him as «Sfântul Ierarh Grigorie Dascălul, Mitropolitul Țării Românești (1765-1834)»; his own life gives 1823–1834 as his years in the see and no year of death.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 22 iunie — «Sfântul Ierarh Grigorie Dascălul, Mitropolitul Țării Românești»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Γρηγόριος ο Διδάσκαλος ο Βατοπαιδινός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and its heading «(1765 - 1834)» is exactly the bracket the folder's `dates` already hold. It is plainly the same man against the corpus's many Gregories: born at Bucharest in 1765 and baptised George, George Minculescu, schooled at the princely academy of St Sabbas, tonsured at Neamț in 1790 under Paisius Velichkovsky, a translator of the fathers out of Latin and Greek, afterwards metropolitan of Wallachia, and buried at the monastery of Căldărușani in Romania. The Greek byname the page gives him, «ο Βατοπαιδινός», of Vatopedi, is new beside the Romanian «Dascălul»; the page also dates his glorification to 21 May 2006, at the liturgy served by the patriarch Teoctist. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn under his line.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).
